doc.title: Frank Alkyer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Orleans, Louisiana, January 10, 2020

chapter: The future and craft of jazz writing
title: Predicting where jazz is heading in the streaming era
summary: Alkyer expects more electronic and crossover music, like Robert Glasper's, and says streaming frees artists from record companies.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Do you also have a prediction about what the music might sound like?

I think that you will get much more — there’ll be — it’ll sound like many things. You will have a group of people who are just as you said trad jazz, that’s a bebop focus, you’re going to have an element of people who are really into technology, so I think we’ll see a lot more electronic improvised music that people will say is not jazz. Is it? Is it not? Leave that up for the debate. I think you’ll see more of that. But one of the most freeing things for jazz artists about the streaming era is, they’re not really making money on CDs so they can make their statement any way they want. They don’t have a bunch of record companies that are telling them how to make the records, so they’re making records they want. And a lot of them are saying, “I don’t want to be known as just a jazz artist, I want

to be known as an artist.” And so we have to go along with that too. I think you’re going to see a lot more crossover kind of thing with like a Robert Glasper, along those lines. And people who are bringing in the elements of hip hop or soul or country or whatever it might be. You’re just going to see that expand exponentially.
